title: Exploring Generative AI Policies in Higher Education: A Comparative Perspective from China, Japan, Mongolia, and the USA

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative Comparative Analysis (QCA) of national AI education policies to assess how governments address the digital poverty gap, resource access, and the educational digital divide between urban and rural areas as well as the Global North and South.

Comparative analysis of national policy documents to evaluate directives on eliminating algorithmic discrimination, addressing training data biases, and promoting diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) across demographic factors.

Policy discourse analysis evaluating the risks of Western-centric Generative AI models overlooking local cultural characteristics and the need for regulations that support local contexts in global education.

Evaluating the policy implications of Generative AI models predominantly trained on English-language data and assessing the need to incorporate local linguistic characteristics into educational AI frameworks.
